Definition: neuter of the comparative of the same as G3122; (adverbially) more (in a greater degree) or rather:--+ better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather.
BiblicalUsage: Mallon means more, rather, much more, and it is the word for choosing the better thing. Romans 5:9 says much more then, being now justified by His blood, we shall be saved from wrath through Him, and Hebrews 11:25 says Moses chose rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season, while Matthew 6:26 asks, are ye not much better than the fowls of the air?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the much more in Romans 5:9 is the logic of grace: if God did the hard part while I was His enemy, He will surely finish it now that I am His.
